turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've got chicken thighs, a bag of spinach and some rice. The kids are hungry and I'm tired.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You could do a quick garlic chicken and rice bowl, or a creamy spinach chicken in one pan. Which sounds better tonight?

contexts.pending: rice bowl or creamy one-pan chicken
think_reask: Okay, time's up. Garlic chicken rice bowl, or the creamy spinach chicken?
So what's it going to be for dinner, the rice bowl or the one-pan creamy chicken?
Have you decided between the two chicken dishes?
welcome_back: Welcome back! We were picking dinner, the rice bowl or the creamy spinach chicken?
Hi again. Still deciding between the garlic chicken bowl and the creamy one-pan version?
There you are. So, which chicken dish for the kids tonight?

endings.user: The rice bowl. The kids won't eat anything creamy with green bits in it.
endings.moshi: Fair enough. Start the rice first, it takes about twenty minutes, and fry the chicken while it cooks.

endings.user: Let's do the creamy one, less washing up.
endings.moshi: Good call. Brown the chicken, then add garlic, cream and the spinach right at the end so it just wilts.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My in-laws are coming Sunday and I want to make something impressive but not stressful.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A slow roast is hard to mess up. Would you rather do a roast chicken, a lamb shoulder, or a vegetarian lasagna?

contexts.pending: roast chicken, lamb shoulder or vegetarian lasagna
think_reask: Alright, have you thought it over? Roast chicken, lamb shoulder or the lasagna?
So, for Sunday with your in-laws, which one are you leaning towards?
welcome_back: Welcome back. You were choosing a main for Sunday, chicken, lamb or lasagna?
Good to have you back. Any thoughts on what to cook for your in-laws?

endings.user: I think the lamb. My father-in-law loves lamb.
endings.moshi: Then lamb it is. Rub it with garlic and rosemary and give it about four hours low and slow.

endings.user: Lasagna, actually. I can make it the day before.
endings.moshi: Smart, it's even better the next day. Just bake it for about forty minutes before they arrive.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm trying to meal prep lunches for the week. Cheap and not boring, please.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sure. Do you want one big batch of the same thing, like a chili, or two smaller recipes you can alternate?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hmm, good question.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: No rush, it really depends on how much variety you need.

contexts.pending: one big batch or two alternating recipes
think_reask: So, one big batch of chili, or two recipes to switch between?
Have you decided how you want to do your lunches, one batch or two?
welcome_back: Welcome back! We were planning your lunches. One big batch or two smaller recipes?
Hey, you're back. Did you decide between one batch and two alternating recipes?

endings.user: Two, I'd get sick of chili by Wednesday.
endings.moshi: Makes sense. How about a lentil curry and a pasta salad, both keep well for four days.

endings.user: One big batch, I really don't have time.
endings.moshi: Then chili is perfect. One pot, five portions, and it freezes well if you make extra.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, do we still have garlic or did you use the last of it?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: I think there's half a bulb in the cupboard by the kettle.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Half a bulb won't be enough. Could you grab some on your way back from work?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Sure, anything else while I'm there?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe a lemon. And check if they have fresh parsley.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Got it, garlic, lemon, parsley.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you taste this sauce? Is it too salty?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Hmm, a little bit. Not terrible though.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ugh, I knew it. I added the stock and forgot it was already salted.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Just throw in some more tomatoes, that usually fixes it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good idea. Do you know if we have another tin?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Bottom shelf, behind the beans.

turns.text: {friend}, are you eating with us tonight or are you going out?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: I'm staying in. What are you making?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Some kind of stir fry, I haven't fully decided. Do you eat mushrooms now?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Only if they're cooked properly, not the slimy kind.

turns.text: Fine, I'll fry them hard on high heat then.

turns.speaker: friend

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How long do I boil an egg if I want the yolk still runny?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: About six minutes from when the water is boiling. Then put it straight into cold water so it stops cooking.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And if I want it a bit firmer, like jammy?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Go for seven to eight minutes. The yolk will be soft but not runny.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay. I was going to put them on toast but / maybe I'll make a ramen bowl instead.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Jammy eggs are great in ramen. Peel them and soak them in soy sauce and a little sugar for an hour if you have time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: An hour is fine. Does it need to go in the fridge?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, keep them in the fridge while they soak. They'll keep for about two days like that.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I have half a pumpkin left over from the weekend. What can I do with it?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Pumpkin soup is the easy win. Roast it with an onion, then blend it with stock and a splash of cream.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Soup sounds nice. Can I freeze it?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, it freezes really well. Just leave the cream out and add it when you reheat.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What spices go with pumpkin? I don't want it to taste like dessert.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Try cumin, smoked paprika and a pinch of chili. A little ginger works too if you like it warming.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've got all of those except ginger / oh wait, there's some powder in the back.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Powder is fine. Use about half a teaspoon, it's stronger than fresh.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Quick one. What can I use instead of buttermilk in pancakes?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Mix a cup of regular milk with a tablespoon of lemon juice or vinegar and let it sit for five minutes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh nice, I have lemons. Will the pancakes taste lemony?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not really. The amount is small and it mostly just helps them rise and stay fluffy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Cool. My daughter wants chocolate chips in them. Do I mix them into the batter?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Better to sprinkle them on top right after you pour the batter in the pan. That way they don't all sink and burn.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Smart. And how hot should the pan be? Mine always come out / kind of pale and then burnt.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Medium heat, no higher. Wait until bubbles pop on the surface before flipping, usually about two minutes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm retired now and finally have time to learn to cook properly. Where should I start?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Congratulations! I'd start with knife skills and a few basics, like a good omelette, a simple soup and a roast.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Knife skills, really? I've been chopping onions for forty years.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then you're ahead already. Still, learning to dice quickly and safely makes every recipe more fun.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Fair. What about a cookbook? I'd rather have / something on paper than a screen.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A classic all-round cookbook is a good start. Look for one that explains why things work, not just the steps.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And maybe a class? There's a community center nearby.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A class is a lovely idea. You'll learn faster with someone watching your technique, and you'll meet people too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Alright, I'll call them tomorrow.
